Pilot village report. The pilot village received 320 millimetres of rainfall during the monsoon season, which was above the district average. Volunteers visited each household twice a month to record water usage. The team trained twelve local technicians to maintain the hand pumps. Soil samples were collected from fifteen plots and sent to the district laboratory. Community meetings were held in the school yard every second Friday. A small library of farming leaflets was placed in the village office. Seed packets were distributed free of charge to families with less than one acre of land. The drainage channels along the main road were cleared before the rains began. Two storage sheds were built to keep fertiliser dry during the monsoon. Women's groups organised a weekly market for vegetables grown in home gardens. The mobile clinic visited on the first Tuesday of every month. A weather board outside the office displayed the daily forecast for farmers. Teachers received a short course on keeping simple records of crop yields. The committee reviewed the progress reports at the end of each quarter. Fishermen were given advice on keeping ponds clean and stocking the right fish.
